learn.hook: If you said one number every second, day and night, it would take you about 116 days to reach 1 crore!
points: Indian places from the right: ones, tens, hundreds, thousands, ten thousands, lakhs, ten lakhs, crores, ten crores.
In the Indian system we put the first comma after 3 digits from the right, then a comma after every 2 digits.
The value of a digit = the digit × the value of its place.

steps: 3 is in the crore place, 45 is in the lakh periods, 07 is thousands, 210 is the rest
So it is 3 crore, 45 lakh, 7 thousand, 210
example.answer: Three crore forty-five lakh seven thousand two hundred ten

learn.reallife: Prices of houses, the number of people in a city and money spent by the government are all told in lakhs and crores in the news.

games.title: Match the number to its name

quiz.q: How many thousands make one lakh?
quiz.explain: 1 lakh is 1,00,000. Divide by 1,000 and you get 100. So 100 thousands make a lakh.
quiz.mistake: Thinks each new place name is just 10 times the previous one

quiz.q: How many lakhs make one crore?
quiz.mistake: Confuses ten lakh with one crore

quiz.q: A cricket stadium holds 45,000 fans. How many such full stadiums make 9 lakh fans?
quiz.mistake: Loses or adds a zero while dividing

quiz.q: Which shows 5 crore 6 lakh in digits?
quiz.explain: 5 goes in the crore place and 6 lakh is 06 in the lakh periods: 5,06,00,000.
quiz.mistake: Puts 6 in the ten lakh place instead of the lakh place

quiz.q: What is the place value of 7 in 4,73,15,020?
quiz.explain: In 4,73,15,020 the 7 is in the ten lakh place, so its value is 7 × 10,00,000 = 70,00,000.
quiz.mistake: Reads the 7 as being in the lakh place

quiz.q: Riya's school wants to collect ₹10,00,000 for a Diwali charity drive. It has ₹2,40,000 so far. How much more is needed?
quiz.explain: Subtract what they have from the target: 10,00,000 − 2,40,000 = 7,60,000.
quiz.mistake: Adds instead of subtracting, or slips while borrowing

quiz.q: How many zeros are there in 1 crore written in digits?
quiz.explain: 1 crore = 1,00,00,000. Count the zeros: 7.
quiz.mistake: Counts the zeros of 10 lakh (6) instead

quiz.q: Which is larger: 98 lakh or 1 crore?
quiz.explain: 1 crore is 100 lakh, and 100 lakh is more than 98 lakh.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the bigger-looking number 98 must mean the bigger amount

teach.ask: Tweet tweet! Gappu heard the word 'crore' on TV. What are a lakh and a crore, and how are they connected?
teach.praise: Wow! Now Gappu can read the big numbers in the newspaper!
teach.nudge: But how many lakhs fit inside one crore?

learn.hook: A cricket video can have '2 million views' or '20 lakh views' — and both mean exactly the same!
points: International system: put a comma after every 3 digits from the right, like 1,250,000.
Its place names are thousand, million and billion.
The number does not change — only the commas and the names change.

example.q: Write 7,25,00,000 in the international system and read it.
steps: Put commas every 3 digits from the right: 72,500,000

learn.reallife: News from other countries, phone app downloads and world population numbers usually use millions and billions.

quiz.q: 1 million is equal to how many lakh?
quiz.explain: 1 million = 10,00,000 in Indian commas, which is 10 lakh.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a million and a lakh are about the same size

quiz.q: 1 billion is equal to how many crore?
quiz.explain: 1 billion = 1,00,00,00,000 in Indian commas = 100 crore.
quiz.mistake: Guesses 1,000 because a billion is 1,000 million

quiz.q: Write 4,500,000 using Indian commas.
quiz.explain: 4,500,000 is 4.5 million = 45 lakh, written 45,00,000.
steps: Then group in twos from the right: 45 | 00 | 000
quiz.mistake: Adds an extra zero while moving the commas

quiz.q: India has about 140 crore people. About how many billion is that?
quiz.explain: 1 billion = 100 crore. So 140 crore = 140 ÷ 100 = 1.4 billion.
quiz.mistake: Thinks 1 billion = 10 crore

quiz.q: How do you read 30,500,000 in the international system?
quiz.explain: Group by threes: 30 | 500 | 000. That is 30 million and 500 thousand.
quiz.mistake: Reads the first group 30 as 3, or mixes up the groups of three

quiz.q: A cricket video has 2.5 million views. How many lakh views is that?
quiz.explain: 1 million = 10 lakh, so 2.5 million = 2.5 × 10 = 25 lakh.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a million and a lakh are the same

quiz.q: Which is the international form of 9,08,76,543?
quiz.explain: The digits are 90876543. Commas every 3 from the right give 90,876,543.
steps: Group in threes from the right: 90 | 876 | 543
quiz.mistake: Drops or adds a digit while regrouping

quiz.q: Which is greater: 50 lakh or 5 million?
quiz.explain: 1 million = 10 lakh, so 5 million = 50 lakh. They are the same number: 5,000,000.
quiz.mistake: Compares only the numbers 50 and 5 and ignores the place names

teach.ask: Gappu's cousin from abroad says 'a million'. Gappu only knows lakhs! How are millions and lakhs connected?
teach.praise: Super! Gappu can now chat in both number languages!
teach.nudge: How many lakh are there in one million? And where do the commas go?

learn.hook: How many laddoos are made in a city for Diwali? Nobody counts every one — we estimate!
points: To estimate is to find a close, easy number instead of the exact one.
To round, look at the digit just right of the place you want. If it is 5 or more, round up; if less than 5, round down.
Round to the nearest ten, hundred, thousand or lakh depending on how close you need to be.
To estimate a sum, difference or product, round each number first and then calculate.
An estimate can be a little more or a little less than the exact answer.

example.q: Estimate 48,760 + 31,290 by rounding each to the nearest thousand.

learn.reallife: Shopkeepers estimate the total bill, and railways estimate how many people travel during festival season.

games.title: True or false?
items: 3,49,999 rounded to the nearest lakh is 3,00,000.
The ten-thousands digit is 4, which is less than 5, so we round down.
6,500 rounded to the nearest thousand is 6,000.
The hundreds digit is 5, so we round up to 7,000.
An estimate is always bigger than the exact answer.
An estimate can be a bit more or a bit less than the exact answer.
49 is close to 50 and 398 is close to 400.
7,95,000 rounded to the nearest lakh is 8,00,000.
The ten-thousands digit is 9, so we round up.

quiz.q: Round 67,482 to the nearest thousand.
quiz.explain: Look at the hundreds digit: 4. It is less than 5, so we round down to 67,000.
steps: Thousands digit is 7, next digit is 4
quiz.mistake: Rounds up just because the number has big digits after the thousands

quiz.q: Round 3,46,915 to the nearest lakh.
quiz.explain: The digit after the lakh place is 4 (ten thousands). 4 < 5, so round down to 3,00,000.
quiz.mistake: Looks at the wrong digit when deciding to round up or down

quiz.q: Round 8,49,999 to the nearest lakh.
quiz.explain: Only the digit right after the lakh place matters. It is 4, so we round down to 8,00,000, even though many 9s follow.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the 9s at the end make the number round up

quiz.q: Arjun's town has 4,87,300 people and the next town has 3,12,450. Round each to the nearest lakh and estimate the total.
quiz.mistake: Works out the exact sum instead of an estimate

quiz.q: Estimate 48 × 512 by rounding 48 to the nearest ten and 512 to the nearest hundred.
quiz.mistake: Loses a zero when multiplying round numbers

quiz.q: A train carries about 1,200 passengers on each trip. About how many passengers travel in 250 trips?
quiz.explain: 1,200 × 250 = 3,00,000. That is about 3 lakh passengers.
quiz.mistake: Counts the zeros wrongly

quiz.q: Which number gives 5,00,000 when rounded to the nearest lakh?
quiz.explain: 4,62,000 has 6 in the ten-thousands place, so it rounds up to 5,00,000. 4,38,000 rounds down to 4,00,000 and 5,51,000 rounds up to 6,00,000.
quiz.mistake: Picks any number that starts with 5

quiz.q: Meena estimated 7,890 − 2,140 by rounding each number to the nearest thousand. What estimate did she get?
quiz.mistake: Gives the exact difference instead of the estimate

teach.ask: Gappu wants to round 3,62,000 to the nearest lakh but is stuck. How do you decide whether to round up or down?
teach.praise: Hooray! Gappu rounded 3,62,000 to 4,00,000 all by himself!
teach.nudge: Which digit do we look at, and what number decides if we go up?
